record.paper_title: FPT Suspects and Tough Customers: Open Problems of Downey and Fellows
record.context_brief: Planar directed feedback vertex set algorithms
record.original_question: Is there a single-exponential fixed-parameter algorithm for Directed Feedback Vertex Set on planar directed graphs, where the parameter is the size k of the feedback vertex set?

evidence.quote:
It remains open if there exist a single exponential algorithm forDirected Feedback Vertex
Set even on planar graphs.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G = (V, E) be a planar directed graph and let k be a positive integer. A directed feedback vertex set of G is a subset S ⊆ V such that the induced subdigraph G[V \ S] is acyclic (contains no directed cycle). The Planar Directed Feedback Vertex Set problem asks, given (G, k), whether G has a directed feedback vertex set of size at most k.

An algorithm for this problem is called fixed-parameter tractable (FPT) with parameter k if it runs in time f(k) · n^{O(1)}, where n = |V| and f is a computable function. It is called single-exponential if f(k) = 2^{O(k)}.

Question: Does there exist a single-exponential fixed-parameter algorithm for Directed Feedback Vertex Set on planar directed graphs, i.e., an algorithm that decides the problem in time 2^{O(k)} · n^{O(1)}?
artifact.category_tag: Parameterized algorithms / directed feedback vertex set
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches indicate that while subexponential FPT algorithms are known for the undirected planar Feedback Vertex Set, and Directed Feedback Vertex Set is FPT in general (with running times like 4^k · k! · n^{O(1)}), there is no published single-exponential 2^{O(k)} · n^{O(1)} algorithm for Directed Feedback Vertex Set on planar digraphs parameterized by solution size. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Pushing the frontiers of subexponential FPT time for Feedback Vertex Set
status_evidence.snippet: Recent results on subexponential FPT algorithms for Feedback Vertex Set on various graph classes; directed planar case not addressed with single-exponential bound.
status_evidence.claim: No single-exponential FPT algorithm for planar Directed Feedback Vertex Set is reported.

status_evidence.title: On Directed Feedback Vertex Set parameterized by treewidth
status_evidence.snippet: For planar digraphs, DFVS parameterized by treewidth t admits 2^{O(t)} n^{O(1)} algorithms; parameterization by solution size on planar digraphs is not stated to be single-exponential.
status_evidence.claim: Single-exponential dependence is known in t (treewidth) for planar DFVS, not in k (solution size).
